Issued at 133 PM EDT Tue Sep 29 2026

Upper-level clouds continue to infiltrate the U.P. from the west via 
troughing moving in from two deep lows today, with one passing 
through northern Canada towards Hudson Bay and the other over the 
Desert Southwest lifting off of the Southern Rockies on Wednesday. 
While a shortwave low riding along the aforementioned Canadian low's 
cold front is bringing rain showers over NE MN and northern WI, 
expect light rainfall to eventually make its way into the western 
U.P. by late this afternoon/early this evening as the shortwave 
continues northeastward towards Hudson Bay and the front progs east 
while weakening. With some subtle WAA being seen ahead of the cold 
front today, temperatures have once again become mild and pleasant 
like they have been over the past several days; expect highs 
generally in the lower to mid 70s across the U.P. by the mid-
afternoon hours even despite the cloud cover. As the shortwave 
nudges by us and the cold front moves overhead tonight, expect the 
rain chances to move through the entire U.P. save for maybe the far 
east by the Soo. However, given the split flow at the synoptic 
level, rainfall amounts look to be light tonight, with most of the 
area looking to get only a tenth of an inch if even that. That being 
said, with some of the better forcing and training further down into 
the south central (as the cold front stalls out), we could see over 
a quarter inch of rainfall in Menominee County; as of the time of 
this writing, the NBM shows a general 40 to 75% chance that the U.P. 
(except the south central) will receive over a tenth of an inch of 
rainfall between this evening and the end of the day Wednesday, 
whereas the south central has a 50 to 90% chance of exceeding a 
quarter inch (highest by the city of Menominee). While there may be 
some training of light rain over the south central and east 
Wednesday into Thursday, guidance continues to slide the 
precipitation further to the south and east, which means we can 
expect almost the entirety U.P. to stay dry now for the mid-week. 

Behind the precipitation on Wednesday, with guidance now suggesting 
a break between the stalled out cold front and a second cold front 
moving through on Thursday, we can expect to see warm temperatures 
with highs in the 70s and pleasant (but cloudy) Fall weather again 
across the U.P. on Wednesday as another round of WAA works across 
the area ahead of the arrival of the second cold front. While the 
second cold front brings cooler/more-normal Fall-like temperatures 
with it from Thursday onwards, again, expect the area to (most 
likely) remain dry. In addition, the projected winds behind the cold 
front on Thursday are now lower than what they were previously 
forecasted to be; only west-northwest wind gusts up to around 30 mph 
are now expected along the Lake Superior shoreline. 

Moving into late this week through this weekend, expect high 
pressure ridging to develop over the Northern Plains before passing 
by the Great Lakes Friday night and Saturday. This should bring high 
temperatures into the 50s and 60s while lows during the overnight 
hours drop down into the 30s to potentially 20s in spots over the 
interior areas. Given the lack of cloud cover expected from the high 
pressure ridging, we could see widespread frost develop during the 
overnight hours pre-dawn Friday morning and especially Friday night. 
Behind this stretch of clearer skies, we could see rain showers 
return via a Clipper skirting through the Upper Midwest into 
northern Ontario late Saturday into Sunday; with 850mb temperatures 
dropping down to -3 to -5C behind the Clipper, I wouldn't be 
surprised if some lake effect drizzle/rain showers developed over 
the northwest wind belts behind it on Sunday. That being said, the 
lake effect rain showers may not last all that long as medium range 
guidance shows more shortwave ridging moving into the area as soon 
as Sunday afternoon, remaining over the Upper Great Lakes through 
early next week.
